speaker: alice
text: Let's start green because nature's been absolutely showing off lately. <cite index='8-18,8-21'>Monarch butterflies in Mexico are having their best year in decades - they're now occupying 7.24 acres, which is up 64% from last winter.</cite> We're talking millions of these gorgeous orange beauties making that epic 2,800-mile journey from Canada and the US.

speaker: charlie
text: <cite index='8-22'>The best part is that forest degradation in their habitat has fallen significantly thanks to sustained conservation efforts.</cite> It's proof that when we actually stick with conservation programs, they work. Sometimes nature just needs us to give it a proper chance to bounce back.

speaker: alice
text: And speaking of comebacks, <cite index='8-26,8-27'>New Zealand's kakapo - one of the world's rarest birds with just 235 adults - has just smashed their breeding record with over 100 chicks hatching this year.</cite> <cite index='8-28'>Get this, vets were even performing CPR on struggling chicks to help them through, and it actually worked!</cite> That's dedication right there.
